focused_after_late_changes.command: bash scripts/db-test.sh -p synveda-store -p synveda-cli --test tenant_lifecycle --test keys --test tenant_erasure --no-fail-fast -- --nocapture

erasure_cases.plan: crates/synveda-store/tests/tenant_lifecycle.rs: the plan derived from the live catalogue places each of the 114 erased tables in exactly one unit and every referencing table no later than its parent across more than 100 checked foreign keys
erasure_cases.guards: the database owner naming a suspended tenant still meets the append-only guard; the ordinary role naming an erasing tenant is not authorized; custody refuses an erasing tenant; KEK replacement lists only active and suspended tenants
erasure_cases.lease: worker A deletes and stops without releasing its lease; worker B is refused erasure_in_progress while the lease is live, reclaims it after expiry as attempt 2, worker A is refused erasure_lease_lost, B finishes; deleted_rows equals the pre-erasure count and an erased rerun returns the identical receipt
erasure_cases.cli_populated: crates/synveda-cli/tests/tenant_erasure.rs, beside a populated canary: tenant root, workspace, project, principal scope and identity, a Session with three events and projections, a Knowledge item with two revisions, a source and an embedding, a policy pack, a console login, a provisioned key and sealed secret; one revision hidden from every role by unproven lineage
erasure_cases.cli_refusals: erasure_unacknowledged without --fixture-rules, tenant_not_suspended for an active tenant, erasure_timeout for a one-second run, tenant_erasing for resume, suspend and archive export while erasing, tenant_erased for resume and suspend afterwards

cli_receipt.note: from the focused run; per-table deletions equal the pre-erasure inventory plus the hidden revision; retained audit rows are counted before tenant.erased is chained

erasure_cases.cli_after: status erased with an empty name; every erased table reads zero; the chain verifies and ends tenant.suspended, tenant.erasure.started, tenant.erased with the receipt digest; the canary's inventory, status and console custody are unchanged; a rerun prints the same digest with changed=false
erasure_cases.cli_hold: a revision with legal_hold refuses erasure_held, adds only one blocked operation and one tenant.erasure.held event, leaves the tenant suspended and resumable

wrappers.compose_fake_docker: scripts/compose-lifecycle.test.mjs: compose.sh tenant forwards suspend to tenant-lifecycle without archive files or a writer stop; refuses missing, unknown, metacharacter and glob arguments and a missing archive directory; archive import stops gateway and worker, runs tenant-archive and recreates them, without printing the administrator URL
wrappers.compose_real_render: real Compose renders tenant-lifecycle with only the migrator URL and KEK on synveda-data, read-only, and tenant-archive with only the administrator URL and KEK plus the archive mount; gateway, worker and migrate never receive the administrator URL
wrappers.compose_refusal: a refused suspend returns its status, releases the project lock and stops no writer; a refused import recreates gateway and worker, returns the refusal's status, skips the smoke and releases the lock; an import that reports the deadline status leaves the writers stopped and retains the lock
wrappers.compose_suites: 180 compose lifecycle, recovery and entrypoint tests and 51 compose contract tests pass
wrappers.helm: scripts/check-helm-contract.mjs: no Job by default; a suspension Job named synveda-tenant-suspend-1 with backoffLimit 0, the migrator URL file, the closed argument list and no bootstrap credential; its NetworkPolicy; refusals for an unacknowledged erase and a missing tenant; an erase Job with both acknowledgements; chart-lint passes

latency.command: SYNVEDA_ADMISSION_MEASURE_WARMUP=200 SYNVEDA_ADMISSION_MEASURE_SAMPLES=4000 bash scripts/db-test.sh -p synveda-gateway --test tenant_admission_measure -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
latency.conditions: debug build, same host, fresh fixture per round, 200 warm-up iterations, 4000 samples per loop, branch and main 4fbd8b2b alternated with the same measurement file; the eligibility loop counts 24 revisions, 6 hidden by unproven lineage, through the restrictive policy that 0015 widens; the ordinary suite runs the eligibility loop with 2 warm-up and 5 samples
latency.conclusion: no change detectable above run-to-run variance on either side; main round 2 was the noisiest. The eligibility read costs about 224 ms per 24-row count on main as well; that is an existing cost of the restrictive policy, recorded here and not introduced by 0015. Not a production latency objective
latency.excluded: a first branch round 2 ran after main shared the build directory and compiled main's crates; it is discarded and repeated after a clean rebuild
latency.attribution: each round's fixture migration names its head: branch rounds migrate to 0015 and main rounds to 0014
